prompt:
EDIT / IDENTITY-PRESERVE.
Image 1 is the ONLY authoritative character design and proportions and is the sheet to remake. Image 2 is a MOTION REFERENCE ONLY for hand-to-chin, head tilt and blinking. Do not import its changed face, proportions, dress, ornament, colors or rendering.
Deliver one professional 2D FULL-BODY animation sprite atlas: EXACTLY 24 cells in 6 equal columns x 4 equal rows, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Landscape 4:3 canvas, aim 2304 x 1728 pixels. Every cell has identical canvas size and character scale. Genuine transparent alpha outside the figures. NO grid, NO numbers, NO text, NO floor, NO shadow, NO background or checkerboard. Generous alpha-zero padding in every cell; full horns, ahoge, wings, hair, fingers, skirt, tail and shoes are always inside its cell.
Character must look EXACTLY like Image 1: the same very compact small chibi silver-white dragon girl, large round head and tiny short body and legs, identical little face with violet eyes, soft lavender shaded long curly silver-white hair, identical parted bangs and one curved ahoge. Same short segmented grey-white horns, pointed ears, flower/knot ornament on SCREEN RIGHT of her head, small pale lavender bat wings. Same elaborate white OFF-SHOULDER fitted dress, broad loose white hanging sleeves, layered ruffled long side skirt with SHORT OPEN FRONT showing the short legs, same waist flower, silver-lavender ribbons and pendant accents, leg strap, white little shoes. Same thick curved white SCALED TAIL extending to SCREEN RIGHT. Trace the design of the first figure in Image 1; NO redesign, no simplification, no dress replacement, no long adult body, no giant skirt hiding legs, no detached limb pieces. These are 24 finished WHOLE character paintings, never a puppet-parts sheet.
Lock orthographic FRONTAL camera, fixed zoom, common centered torso and common shoe baseline for all24 frames. Hair volume, skull size, eye spacing, shoulder width, torso size, waist and leg length remain constant. Maintain identical outlines, shading shapes and accessory locations across neighboring frames. Only the specified small pose motion changes. Keep both shoes planted, no bouncing or scaling.
Animation: gentle THINKING loop, about2 seconds. Both hands start in the relaxed low open pose of Image 1 with a tiny natural up/down sway. Her RIGHT arm (on SCREEN LEFT) bends naturally at the elbow and raises the SAME hand to her chin. Head tilts very slightly toward that hand, max4 degrees, no torso lean. The other arm stays down with subtle motion. Anatomically connected shoulder-elbow-wrist, exactly two arms/hands, fingers not elongated. Slight sleeve/hair/tail follow-through, very small.
Frame schedule (continuous tiny increments, not pose jumps):
1 relaxed neutral; 2 hand starts up; 3 hand at about20% lift; 4 about40%; 5 about65%; 6 about85%.
7 fingertips gently touch chin; 8 subtle head tilt and hand settles, eyes open; 9 eyelids half close; 10 both eyes closed for a brief blink; 11 eyes half open; 12 eyes fully open.
13-16 keep thoughtful gentle tilted-head hand-to-chin pose with tiny breath and other hand sway, same face and dress details.
17 begin un-tilting head and lowering hand; 18 hand90%; 19 hand70%; 20 hand50%; 21 hand30%; 22 hand15%; 23 hand5%; 24 nearly the exact neutral frame1, so the next1 is seamless.
Every next frame is a tiny continuation. Facial identity, hairline, costume panels, tail scales and lighting must NOT fluctuate. No row-by-row changes to body size or pose viewpoint. Prioritize exact first-image likeness and temporal consistency over exaggerated motion.
